A real workstation, with a target to meet

ASUS detailed Gallop on November 13. The fixed-base, two-arm robot is learning motherboard-accessory packing at a group factory: 15 small parts, many in thin transparent bags. The target is 99.5% success within 20 seconds per board, not a published result already achieved.

From worker demonstrations to robot practice

The team starts with open models and recordings from consenting workers wearing cameras. Simulation adds variations, while operators use VR headsets and gloves to teach with actual parts. Planning, supervision, manipulation skills and motion control form separate layers running on an onboard NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor.

Pilots before commercial availability

ASUS plans to add its own tactile hand and a wheeled base, conduct customer pilots in 2027 and target market availability in the second half of 2028. Existing-workstation compatibility and replaceable AI models matter for electronics manufacturing. The announcement does not establish full-shift reliability or achievement of the cycle-time target.
